key_insight: Introduce a lightweight 'memory caching' mechanism that lets recurrent networks grow and retain past context like Transformers, achieving transformer-style long-range recall while keeping subquadratic compute and memory costs.
problem_solved: Addresses the trade-off between Transformers' strong long-context recall but quadratic cost and recurrent architectures' efficiency but poor recall on long/hard retrieval tasks.
method: Attach an append-only cache (growable external memory) to an RNN so past hidden states can be stored and selectively revisited without full quadratic attention.
Use efficient indexing/aggregation (e.g., keys + compressed summaries or sparse retrieval) so reads from the cache are subquadratic and compatible with streaming/incremental processing.
Combine caching reads with standard RNN updates so the model learns when to write, retain, and attend to distant context for recall-heavy tasks.
impact: Provides a practical pathway to get Transformer-like long-range memory with much lower compute and memory overhead, enabling scalable sequence modeling in streaming, low-resource, and real-time applications.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: RNN core with an append-only cache and read/write pathways, annotated with cost per step.
Complexity comparison chart: quadratic Transformer vs cached-RNN subquadratic vs standard RNN, plotted vs sequence length.
Recall/accuracy vs context length plot showing improved long-range retrieval for cached-RNNs.
Timeline/animation concept: how the cache grows over time and how selective reads retrieve distant information.
paper_title: Memory Caching: RNNs with Growing Memory
paper_authors: Ali Behrouz, Zeman Li, Yuan Deng, Peilin Zhong, Meisam Razaviyayn
